source_text: nos excusationem praebere turpibus et flagitiosis hominibus, ut cum infanda immunda commiserint, contra voluntatem se dicant fecisse, et ideo nullum habere peccatum
pass_a_gloss: We excusationem praebere turpibus and flagitiosis hominibus, so-that/as when/with infanda immunda commiserint, against will himself dicant fecisse, and for-that-reason no to-have sin.

lemmas.lexica: LS peccatum=fault, error; Blaise Christian sin
LS voluntas=will, wish; Blaise moral will

pass_b_english: Augustine reports Julian accused him of offering shameful and criminal people an excuse: after committing unspeakable and unclean acts, they could say they acted against their will and therefore had no sin.

choices.why: Julian's definition of sin is an act of will. Keep 'will' rather than later 'free will' system language unless liberum arbitrium is present.
Julian's forensic/moral fault tied to will, not a substance in nature.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here.
